subject: Commit-term sensitivity: pricing buffers & approval chase for Kestrel Labs
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@kestrellabs.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Reserved capacity ask + pricing sensitivity

Marcus —

Thanks for the demo earlier. Kestrel is looking at a reserved capacity commit to back our next product cycle: estimate ~480 A100-equivalent GPU-months over 12 months (phased). Our procurement team needs to understand how Redwood will handle pricing sensitivity if market GPU costs move materially during the term. Specifically:

- Are discounts locked by commit volume or indexed to spot/market prices?
- Do you offer mid-term price triggers (rebates / credits) or only upfront discounts?
- What approval path do we need if we request a floor/escape clause tied to price spikes?

We can be flexible on term if there are guardrails that limit Redwood's exposure. Can you share a short scenario (best/worst case) for 12m and 24m tenors and any template language you typically include? We need this to brief legal and finance this week.

Attached: high-level usage plan (procurement@kestrellabs.com).

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement deadline is 11/17.

—Aisha
Procurement, Kestrel Labs
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@kestrellabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask + pricing sensitivity

Aisha —

Thanks for the clear ask and the usage plan. I put together a short sensitivity workbook and a straw-term we can start with. See attachments: reserved_capacity_model_v3.xlsx and an initial SLA draft. High-level summary below:

- Proposed initial term: 12 months with a phase-in ramp (month 1-3 at 40% activation, month 4-12 at steady-state).
- Baseline discounted price assumes current procurement cost + 12% Redwood margin.
- Two mitigation options we recommend: (A) fixed discount by commit (no indexation) with a larger upfront discount; (B) index-based protection: commit price + indexation band (+/-) with rebate ladder if market spikes > X%.
- Approval implications: discounts >20% or a contract-level indexation floor require finance + CRO sign-off; indexation language requires Legal review for pass-through clauses.

Karthik / Lauren — looping you in for a quick read. We need a definition of the approval gate and a recommended fallback (e.g., phased rebate vs. credit escrow). Aisha — if you can confirm whether Kestrel prefers fixed discount or indexation, that helps us fast-track.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0193
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 13:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask + pricing sensitivity

Marcus / Lauren —

Quick notes from finance modeling (attached cap_exposure_calc.xlsx):

1) Exposure windows: for a 12m commit with the proposed ramp, our downside (market price spike +30%) increases unit cost by ~27% across the commit. That erodes margin heavily if we grant >18% flat discount.

2) Recommendation: we can approve a staged discount ladder tied to a two-way banded index:
   - Upfront discount: up to 12% guaranteed by commit volume.
   - Rebate ladder: if market index increases 15-30%, rebates convert to credit (future invoices) rather than cash refunds; if >30% spike, automatic review with potential partial term extension or a capped escrow payment.

3) Approval path: discounts <=12%: Sales + Finance OK; discounts between 12%-20%: Sales + Finance + VP Ops sign-off; discounts >20%: require CRO and CFO approval and a risk escrow. Indexation/escape clauses: require Legal + CFO sign-off.

If the customer insists on fully fixed pricing protecting them from any market movement, we should move to shorter tenors (6-12m) or allow lower volume guarantees.

—Karthik
Head of Strategic Finance, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@kestrellabs.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask + pricing sensitivity

Looping in a quick commercial guardrail from Product and Sales Ops perspective.

- We can offer a 12-month pilot with the following commercial guardrails: 12% guaranteed discount by commit, 6% contingent credit ladder if index moves 15-25%, and a capped 3% cash escrow for extreme events (>30%) that kicks a review meeting (no immediate cash payouts).
- Canary / phased capacity: enable a 3-month early termination window between month 3-6 if usage materially undershoots, with a pro-rata refund schedule to reduce Kestrel's downside and our exposure.
- SLA: include 99.9% availability target for reserved pools and a targeted remediation SLA. We will draft SLA language but want to keep credits limited and tied to measurable infra incidents (not market pricing).

If Aisha and procurement@kestrellabs.com confirm those guardrails, we can route the proposal: discount <=12% (Sales + Finance). Anything above that follows Karthik's path.

—Lauren
Director, Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@kestrellabs.com>, procurement@kestrellabs.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:44:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask + pricing sensitivity

Aisha —

Thanks for the patience. Based on internal review we propose the following term sheet for your procurement review (attachments: reserved_capacity_model_v3.xlsx, sla-draft-kestrel.pdf):

Proposal (12-month pilot):
- Commit: 480 GPU-months (phased as discussed).
- Commercial: 12% upfront discount tied to commit volume.
- Contingent protection: two-way index band: if market index increases 15-25% -> apply 6% invoice credit (applied as future credit); if index increases >30% -> trigger a joint review and capped escrow mechanism (3% of total committed value) to be held pending remediation or partial term extension.
- Approval: the above is Sales + Finance approved. Any request to increase the guaranteed discount above 12% will need VP Ops sign-off or CRO/CFO per Karthik's routing.
- Operational guardrails: 3-month early adjustment window (month 3-6) if usage undershoots by >25% with pro-rata reconciliation; 99.9% reserved-pool availability SLA (credits only for infra incidents).

Next steps: if Kestrel is comfortable with the construct, propose a 30-minute call this week to finalize language and route approval. If you prefer a fixed-price (no indexation), flag that and we will re-run scenarios and route for higher-level approvals.

Thanks —
Marcus
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0193
